front: What is git blame in one sentence?
back: Line-level authorship: which commit last touched each line — forensics for regressions, not a performance review weapon.

front: Explain the mental model of git blame (how the system thinks).
back: git blame walks blob history backward via git log -L mechanics — shows last modifying commit per line, not who originally wrote the logic if it moved.

front: Symptom: Blame stops at unrelated commit — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: File rename break · Fix: git log --follow -- file then blame old path

front: Symptom: Line shows wrong date — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Author date vs committer · Fix: git blame --date=iso; git show for details

front: Symptom: Ignore-revs not applied — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Config path · Fix: blame.ignoreRevsFile in repo .git/config or local

front: Symptom: Binary / generated file noise — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Should be gitignored · Fix: Stop blaming; fix .gitattributes export-ignore

front: Symptom: Slow on huge file — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Full history · Fix: -L range; or blame specific commit snapshot

front: Gotcha with git blame: what silently fails?
back: Force-pushed rebased history — blame SHAs won't match old PR discussions; use reflog on maintainer machine if still available.

front: When should you NOT use git blame?
back: Finding why code exists — read commit message + PR + tests; blame only points to where. Binary files — meaningless line blame. Before -M/-C on moved code — you'll chase the wrong commit.

front: What is Git Commands — Recovery & Debug in one sentence?
back: One-line: when history is wrong, refs are lost, or merges surprise you — reflog, bisect, and dry-run merge before you force-push.

front: Explain the mental model of Git Commands — Recovery & Debug (how the system thinks).
back: Git stores a DAG of commits; refs (branches, tags, HEAD) are movable pointers. git reflog records where refs *were* — your safety net after bad reset/rebase. Recovery is almost always possible until garbage collection (gc) prunes unreachable objects (~90 days default).

back: git push --force on shared main — use revert or a coordinated reset window. Bisect on flaky tests — script must be deterministic or bisect lies. Reflog on someone else's machine — recover from your clone or remote tags.

front: What is git rebase in one sentence?
back: Replay your commits on top of a moving base — linear history without merge commits — Pro Git (Chacon); dangerous on shared branches without agreement.

front: Explain the mental model of git rebase (how the system thinks).
back: Rebase copies each commit as a new hash (x', y') with updated parent. Old commits become unreachable (until reflog expires).

front: What are the production-safe defaults for git rebase?
back: During rebase, "ours" = upstream base, "theirs" = your replayed commit — opposite of merge.

front: Gotcha with git rebase: what silently fails?

front: When should you NOT use git rebase?
back: Shared long-lived branch multiple people commit to — merge or trunk-based with short branches. Integrating released tags — don't rewrite history consumers depend on. You need true merge context — complex binary conflicts sometimes easier with one merge commit.

front: What is Git Submodule in one sentence?
back: One-line: pin another repo at a specific commit inside your repo — powerful for vendoring, painful if treated like a shortcut for package management.

front: Explain the mental model of Git Submodule (how the system thinks).
back: A submodule is a gitlink: parent repo records a path + exact commit SHA of nested repo. Cloning parent does not auto-fetch submodule contents unless --recurse-submodules.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Git Submodule?
back: parent-repo/ → vendor/lib/ → commit abc1234 of github.com/org/lib → .gitmodules → URL + path mapping → git clone --recurse-submodules <url> → git submodule update --init --recursive

front: Given a broken Git Submodule setup, what is your first validation command?
back: parent-repo/

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Git Submodule?
back: Creates .gitmodules + gitlink entry.

front: Symptom: Empty directory after clone — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Submodule not initialized · Fix: git submodule update --init --recursive

front: Symptom: "modified content" in git status — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Submodule on different commit than pinned · Fix: Commit new SHA in parent or reset submodule

front: Symptom: Detached HEAD in submodule — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Normal after update · Fix: Checkout branch inside submodule or stay detached at tag

front: Symptom: Push rejected from submodule — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Submodule has own remote · Fix: cd submodule && git push then update parent pointer

front: Symptom: CI checkout missing files — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CI didn't init submodules · Fix: submodules: recursive in GitHub Actions / GIT_SUBMODULE_STRATEGY

front: Symptom: Merge conflict on gitlink — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Both sides bumped submodule · Fix: Pick correct SHA, git add path

front: Gotcha with Git Submodule: what silently fails?
back: Detached HEAD is default inside submodule — easy to commit locally and forget to push submodule remote before updating parent.

front: When should you NOT use Git Submodule?
back: npm/cargo/go modules exist — use proper package manager unless you need to fork/patch at source level. Teams unfamiliar with gitlinks — onboarding cost exceeds benefit for app repos.

back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: parent-repo/

front: What is Git Worktree in one sentence?
back: One-line: multiple checked-out directories sharing one .git object store — review PR and hotfix in parallel without stash churn.

front: Explain the mental model of Git Worktree (how the system thinks).
back: One repository, many working trees. Each worktree has its own index and working directory but shares objects, refs, and config.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Git Worktree?
back: repo/.git/ ← bare or main git dir → repo/ ← worktree 1 (main) → ../repo-feature/ ← worktree 2 (feature branch) → ../repo-hotfix/ ← worktree 3 (detached at tag) → git worktree add ../project-feature feature-branch

front: Given a broken Git Worktree setup, what is your first validation command?
back: repo/.git/ ← bare or main git dir

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Git Worktree?
back: Each linked worktree stores a .git file (not dir) pointing at main repo: gitdir: /path/to/main/.git/worktrees/feature.

front: Symptom: "branch already checked out" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: git worktree list · Fix: One branch per worktree max; use detached or different branch

front: Symptom: Worktree dir deleted manually — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: git worktree list shows prunable · Fix: git worktree prune

front: Symptom: Can't remove — dirty tree — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: git status in worktree · Fix: Commit, stash, or --force remove

front: Symptom: Submodule confusion — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Each worktree needs submodule update · Fix: Run in each checkout separately

front: Symptom: Disk looks duplicated — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Shared objects · Fix: Normal — only working files duplicate

front: Gotcha with Git Worktree: what silently fails?
back: Same branch in two worktrees is forbidden — Git prevents index corruption. Create a temp branch or use detached HEAD.

front: When should you NOT use Git Worktree?
back: Long-term second clone needs — separate clone is simpler if you want different remotes or hooks. Replacing git stash for tiny context switches — stash is lighter for 5-minute detours.

front: What is GPG sign (Git commits & tags) in one sentence?
back: One-line: cryptographically sign Git commits/tags with your GPG key — proves authorship and integrity for supply-chain and release audit. Fix "no secret key" before enabling signing in CI or globally.

front: Explain the mental model of GPG sign (Git commits & tags) (how the system thinks).
back: Git attaches an OpenPGP signature to commit or tag objects. Verifiers use your public key (gpg --list-keys) to confirm the signature matches your identity. Signing requires a private key in your agent's keyring — passphrase-protected by default.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for GPG sign (Git commits & tags)?
back: git commit -S ──► gpg signs hash ──► signature embedded in commit → git log --show-signature ──► gpg --verify against trusted keys → gpg --full-generate-key → gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format=long → git config --global user.signingkey ABC123DEF456

front: Given a broken GPG sign (Git commits & tags) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: git commit -S ──► gpg signs hash ──► signature embedded in commit

front: What are the production-safe defaults for GPG sign (Git commits & tags)?
back: Generate key (if none):

front: Symptom: no default secret key — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: gpg --list-secret-keys · Fix: Generate/import key; set user.signingkey

front: Symptom: Wrong key used — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: git config user.signingkey · Fix: Match long ID from secret keyring

front: Symptom: Passphrase loop over SSH — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: pinentry · Fix: export GPG_TTY=$(tty); use gpg-agent; local sign

front: Symptom: GitHub "Unverified" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Pubkey not uploaded · Fix: Export armor key to GitHub; email must match commit

front: Symptom: CI can't sign — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: No secret in agent · Fix: Use bot key in CI secret store; or sign tags locally only

front: Symptom: error: gpg failed to sign — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: gpg.program wrong · Fix: Point to gpg or gpg2; test `echo test \

front: Gotcha with GPG sign (Git commits & tags): what silently fails?
back: Key in git config but only public key imported — signing needs secret key on that machine.

front: When should you NOT use GPG sign (Git commits & tags)?
back: Internal-only repos with no audit requirement — signing overhead may not pay off. Replace code review — signature proves key holder signed, not that code is safe. Secrets in commits — sign doesn't encrypt; use git-crypt/SOPS for confidentiality.
